# Architecture The Weather Risk Intelligence Agent answers analysts' questions about weather disruption risk at the company's US distribution hubs. The core design rule: **code computes every number, and the LLM only chooses which code to run and explains the results.** ## 1. System overview ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Client UI["Chat UI
web/ (HTML/JS, voice)"] CLI["CLI / curl"] end subgraph API["FastAPI app (app/api)"] CHAT["POST /chat"] DATA["GET /hubs, /rankings,
/hubs/{id}/risk, /methodology"] ALERT["POST /alerts/check
GET /alerts"] end subgraph Agent["Agent (app/agent)"] LOOP["Tool-use loop
Claude Opus 5.5"] TOOLS["7 tools
(Pydantic-validated)"] GROUND["Grounding check"] end subgraph Core["Deterministic core"] SCORE["Scoring engine
(app/scoring + config/scoring.yaml)"] STATS["Weather statistics"] end MON["Alert monitor
(app/alerts, daily APScheduler)"] DB[("SQLite
data/wria.db")] CLAUDE(["Anthropic API"]) OM(["Open-Meteo ERA5"]) FEMA(["FEMA NRI"]) NWS(["NOAA NWS alerts"]) HOOK(["Webhook
(e.g. Slack)"]) UI --> CHAT & DATA & ALERT CLI --> CHAT CHAT --> LOOP LOOP <--> CLAUDE LOOP --> TOOLS --> SCORE & STATS TOOLS -->|live| NWS LOOP --> GROUND DATA --> SCORE ALERT --> MON MON --> SCORE MON --> HOOK SCORE & STATS --> DB LOOP -->|sessions| DB MON -->|snapshots, alerts| DB INGEST["Ingest job
(app/data_sources)"] --> OM & FEMA INGEST --> DB ``` ### Request flow for one chat question 1. The UI sends `POST /chat {message, session_id}`. 2. The agent loads the conversation from SQLite and calls Claude with the system prompt, the history and 7 tool definitions. The JSON schemas of the tools come from Pydantic models. 3. Claude asks for tools (for example `rank_hubs(rank_by="winter", region="Midwest")`). Each tool input is validated by its Pydantic model, then runs deterministic Python. Errors such as an unknown hub go back to Claude as `is_error` results, so it can recover (for example by asking which Portland the user meant). 4. This repeats for up to 8 rounds. The last round has tools turned off, so a reply is guaranteed. 5. The final reply must follow the `AgentAnswer` JSON schema. The API enforces it (`output_config.format`) and Pydantic validates it again. 6. A **grounding check** compares every number in `key_figures` and `ranking` with the tool outputs, and every hub id with the hub registry. Anything unmatched is returned as `grounding_warnings`, which the UI shows. 7. The session is saved only after a valid answer. A failed turn never corrupts the conversation. ## 2. Components | Component | Code | Responsibility | |---|---|---| | Data sources | `app/data_sources/` | HTTP clients for Open-Meteo, FEMA NRI and NWS, with retries and rate-limit waits. The ingest job is idempotent. | | Storage | `app/storage/` | The SQLite schema and queries, and the builder of the starting database (`seed.py`). | | Scoring engine | `app/scoring/` | Pure functions: weather metrics, then hazard scores, then a composite score, tier and rank. Weights and scales are in `config/scoring.yaml`. | | Agent | `app/agent/` | The Claude tool loop, tool registry, output schema, system prompt and grounding check. | | API | `app/api/main.py` | FastAPI endpoints, dependency injection (DB connection, agent) and static UI hosting. | | Chat UI | `web/` | Plain HTML/CSS/JS with no build step. Ranking panel, follow-up chips, voice input and read-aloud. | | Alerts | `app/alerts/` | Re-scores all hubs, compares the result with the last snapshot, and posts the changes to a webhook. Runs daily or on demand. | | Evaluation | `evals/` | 17 cases graded by code, with expected values taken from the engine at run time. | ### The LLM ↔ code contract (JSON schemas) There are two typed boundaries, both defined once in `app/agent/schemas.py`: - **LLM → code (tool inputs).** Each tool's input schema is generated from a Pydantic model with `extra="forbid"`, and uses `Literal` types for hazards and regions. Invalid input is rejected before any code runs. - **LLM → user (final answer).** `AgentAnswer` contains `answer`, `answer_type`, `hubs`, `ranking[]`, `key_figures[]` (each with `source_tool`), `reasoning`, `assumptions`, `data_sources`, `confidence`, `confidence_reason` and `follow_up_suggestions`. This makes assumptions and uncertainty a required part of every answer, not an optional extra. ### Scoring model (summary) The full definition is in `config/scoring.yaml`, and the reasoning is in [PLAN.md](PLAN.md). - **Five hazards:** winter (27%), flood (27%), hurricane and wind (26%), tornado and hail (15%), and heat (5%). Heat gets the lowest weight because it mostly slows work rather than closing a hub. - **Hazard scores.** Each hazard score is a weighted mix of components from two sources: - ERA5 weather counts, such as snow days per year or heavy-rain days; - FEMA NRI annual frequencies. Each component is scaled to 0–100 on a **fixed** range, not min–max across hubs. Then one hub's score changes only when its own data changes, which keeps rankings stable and alerts meaningful. - **Tiers:** High ≥ 60, Elevated ≥ 40, Moderate ≥ 20, Low below 20. - **Fingerprint.** A hash of `scoring.yaml` is stored with each score snapshot, so you can always tell which model produced a number. ## 3. Repository structure ``` app/ api/main.py FastAPI app: chat, data, alert endpoints; serves web/ agent/ agent.py Claude tool-use loop, sessions, CLI tools.py 7 tools wrapping the deterministic core + score cache schemas.py Pydantic models: tool inputs + AgentAnswer output schema prompts.py System prompt (rules: no invented numbers, scope, uncertainty) grounding.py Checks answer numbers/hubs against tool outputs scoring/ engine.py, metrics.py, stats.py, models.py data_sources/ open_meteo.py, fema_nri.py, nws.py, http.py, ingest.py storage/ db.py (schema + queries), seed.py (starting database builder) alerts/ monitor.py (snapshot/diff/notify), scheduler.py (APScheduler) config.py Settings (.env) and hub registry config/ hubs.yaml 21 hubs: id, region, coordinates, county FIPS scoring.yaml Metrics, hazard weights, scales, tiers data/seed/ Committed starting database (copied to data/wria.db on first start) web/ index.html, app.js, styles.css evals/ cases.yaml, grader.py, run.py, baseline.md tests/ Unit + API + eval-harness tests (offline, no API key needed) docs/ PLAN.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, ai-session/ Dockerfile, render.yaml ``` ## 4. Data storage choice: SQLite **Choice:** one SQLite file (`data/wria.db`) in WAL mode. | Table | Contents | |---|---| | `weather_daily` | ~38k rows: one per hub per day for 2021–2025 (snowfall, precipitation, min/max temperature, gusts) | | `nri_county` | FEMA NRI record per county (JSON) | | `chat_sessions` | Full message list per session, so follow-ups keep their context | | `score_snapshots`, `risk_alerts` | Alert history | | `fetch_log` | What was fetched and when | **Why SQLite** - **Size.** The data is small (3.4 MB) and read-heavy, with essentially one writer (the ingest or alert job). A database server would add work to run and no benefit. - **Fast, cheap reads.** Scoring reads a hub's 5 years of weather in milliseconds, and scores are cached in memory after that. - **The data ships with the code.** The committed starting copy (`data/seed/wria-seed.db`) means a fresh clone or container works immediately. It doesn't depend on the free APIs' rate limits, and the numbers are reproducible for evaluation. - **Concurrency.** WAL mode lets the API read while the alert job writes. **Alternatives considered** - *Postgres:* better for many writers or several app instances, but it adds a server to run. - *Parquet/CSV files:* fine for the weather data, but awkward for sessions and alerts. - *Fetching from the APIs on every question:* rejected because it's slow, rate-limited and not reproducible. **When this would change.** Several server instances, or sessions that must survive redeploys on a host with an ephemeral disk, would mean moving `chat_sessions`, `score_snapshots` and `risk_alerts` to a hosted Postgres. The read-only weather and FEMA data could stay as a file. All SQL lives in `app/storage/db.py`, so the change is contained there. ## 5. Deployment - **Container:** `Dockerfile`, built on uv's Python 3.12 slim image. - Dependencies are installed from `uv.lock` (`--frozen`), so versions are pinned. - It runs as a non-root user with a health check on `/health`. - It runs **one worker on purpose:** the alert scheduler runs inside the process, and SQLite has one writer. - **Host:** Render, using `render.yaml`. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set in the dashboard and never stored in git. - **Free-tier limits:** - The service sleeps after about 15 minutes idle, and the daily alert job doesn't run while it's asleep. On a paid plan you'd use a Render cron job calling `python -m app.alerts.monitor`. - The disk is wiped on redeploy. Each deploy starts again from the starting database, so chat sessions and alert history are lost. - **Scaling path:** a hosted database for state, and the alert job moved to an external scheduler so it runs once. After that the API is stateless and can have several replicas. ## 6. Reliability, cost and safety - **LLM failures.** Server-side model fallback is enabled. Refusals, `max_tokens` cut-offs and invalid output raise an `AgentError`, which the API returns as HTTP 502. Each session has a lock, so two messages can't interleave. - **Cost.** - Prompt caching covers the system prompt and tools. - `effort: medium` is used. - The data endpoints (`/rankings` and the others) never call the LLM. - An eval run costs about $1 for 17 cases. - **Honesty.** - The prompt and schema require stated assumptions and a confidence level. - The grounding check catches invented numbers. - Eval cases test unknown hubs, off-topic questions, years with no data, and requests for dollar estimates. ## 7. Known limitations - **Data resolution.** ERA5 is gridded (~25 km), so values are point estimates, not station observations. FEMA NRI is county-level and updated rarely. - **Exposure only.** The score measures exposure to weather, not financial loss, because there is no hub throughput or cost data. - **Judgment calls.** The weights and scales are documented and easy to change, but they are judgment calls, not values fitted to historical outages. - **Live alerts aren't scored.** Live NWS alerts are shown as context only; they are not part of the score.

Ranking panel, follow-up chips, voice input and read-aloud. | | Alerts | `app/alerts/` | Re-scores all hubs, compares the result with the last snapshot, and posts the changes to a webhook. Runs daily or on demand. | | Evaluation | `evals/` | 17 cases graded by code, with expected values taken from the engine at run time. | ### The LLM ↔ code contract (JSON schemas) There are two typed boundaries, both defined once in `app/agent/schemas.py`: - **LLM → code (tool inputs).** Each tool's input schema is generated from a Pydantic model with `extra="forbid"`, and uses `Literal` types for hazards and regions. Heat gets the lowest weight because it mostly slows work rather than closing a hub. - **Hazard scores.** Each hazard score is a weighted mix of components from two sources: - ERA5 weather counts, such as snow days per year or heavy-rain days; - FEMA NRI annual frequencies. Each component is scaled to 0–100 on a **fixed** range, not min–max across hubs. Then one hub's score changes only when its own data changes, which keeps rankings stable and alerts meaningful. - **Tiers:** High ≥ 60, Elevated ≥ 40, Moderate ≥ 20, Low below 20. - **Fingerprint.** A hash of `scoring.yaml` is stored with each score snapshot, so you can always tell which model produced a number. ## 3. Refusals, `max_tokens` cut-offs and invalid output raise an `AgentError`, which the API returns as HTTP 502. content.text:
Stage 9 is committed locally as `f40a573`, not pushed. I couldn't build the Docker image because Docker isn't installed on this Mac, so I checked its steps another way (below). Here's what I did and why.

**`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`**
This covers the architecture document the assignment asks for:
- **System diagram** (Mermaid, which GitHub draws as a picture) and the step-by-step path of one chat question: tools, structured answer, number check, saving the session.
- **The two JSON-schema boundaries** between the LLM and the code: what Claude sends to tools, and the `AgentAnswer` it must return.
- **A short scoring summary**, the repository layout, and **why SQLite**:
  - the data is small and mostly read, with one writer;
  - the data ships with the code, which makes results reproducible;
  - it needs no database server.

  It also covers the alternatives I considered (Postgres, Parquet files, calling the APIs live) and when to switch.
- **Deployment limits, reliability and cost, and known limitations.** Stating the uncertainty is part of the brief.

**`Dockerfile` + `.dockerignore`**
- **Locked dependencies.** Packages install from `uv.lock`, in their own layer, so editing code doesn't re-download them.
- **Only what's needed at runtime.** The image holds the app, config, UI and starting database; tests, evals and docs stay out.
- **Safer defaults.** It runs as a non-root user and has a health check on `/health`.
- **One worker on purpose.** The alert scheduler runs inside the process, and SQLite has one writer.
- **Nothing private.** `.dockerignore` keeps `.env` (your key), your local database and `.git` out of the image.

**`render.yaml`**
- A Render setup file for the free plan, with a health check and automatic redeploys on push.
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is marked secret, so Render asks for it in the dashboard and it never goes into git.

**README**
- **New sections:** "Run with Docker" and "Deploy (Render)", with the free-plan limits and a warning to set an Anthropic spending limit, since a public URL spends your credits.
- **A bug of mine, fixed:** in the last commit I'd accidentally repeated the starting-database paragraph 3 times. It's now once.
- **Removed** the "work in progress" note.

**How I checked it**
- I copied exactly the files the image copies into a clean folder and ran the same install command. That gave a clean install with no dev tools.
- I started the server with the image's exact start command. It created the database from the starting copy, and `/health` showed 38,346 days. The UI, the static files and the health-check command all worked.
- All 83 tests pass.

**For the deployed URL, you'll need to do these steps yourself**, since they use your account and your key:
1. Push this commit.
2. In the Render dashboard, choose **New → Blueprint** and pick the repo.
3. Paste your `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` when Render asks for it.
4. Set a spending limit in the Anthropic Console.

When you have the URL, I can test it live.

"""Turn Claude Code session logs (.jsonl) into a readable, redacted Markdown transcript.

Usage:
    python docs/ai-session/export_session.py OUT_DIR SESSION.jsonl [SESSION2.jsonl ...]
        [--subagent AGENT.jsonl ...]

Writes, for the given session files (in order, as consecutive parts of one session):
    OUT_DIR/transcript.md       every user message, assistant reply and tool call, in order
    OUT_DIR/session.jsonl       the same records as raw JSON (user/assistant only), redacted

What is left out, and why:
  - Harness bookkeeping records (API request blobs, file snapshots, cost state): not part of
    the conversation, large, and they repeat the system prompt.
  - <system-reminder> blocks injected into user turns: automatic context, not the user's words.
  - The model's private reasoning ("thinking" blocks): only the visible conversation is shown.
  - Long tool outputs are cut to their first lines in the Markdown (the raw JSONL keeps
    them whole).

Redaction runs on everything written: API keys, the user's email, name and local username.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

# Replacement rules. Order matters: the full name before the username it contains.
REDACTIONS = [
    (re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}"), "[REDACTED_API_KEY]"),
    (re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@gmail\.com"), "[user-email]"),
    (re.compile(r"[redacted]", re.I), "[user]"),
    (re.compile(r"[redacted]", re.I), "user"),
    (re.compile(r"\b[redacted]1\b", re.I), "[github-user]"),
]
SYSTEM_REMINDER = re.compile(r"<system-reminder>.*?</system-reminder>", re.S)
MAX_RESULT_LINES, MAX_RESULT_CHARS = 40, 4000
MAX_INPUT_LINES = 80


def redact(text: str) -> str:
    for pattern, repl in REDACTIONS:
        text = pattern.sub(repl, text)
    return text


def clip(text: str, max_lines: int, max_chars: int = 10**9) -> str:
    lines = text.splitlines()
    out = "\n".join(lines[:max_lines])[:max_chars]
    hidden = len(lines) - max_lines
    if hidden > 0 or len(text) > max_chars:
        out += f"\n… [{max(hidden, 0)} more lines cut for readability; full text in session.jsonl]"
    return out


def fence(text: str, lang: str = "") -> str:
    # Use a fence longer than any backtick run inside, so nested code blocks can't break it.
    ticks = "`" * max(3, max((len(m) for m in re.findall(r"`+", text)), default=0) + 1)
    return f"{ticks}{lang}\n{text}\n{ticks}"


def load_records(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        try:
            rec = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if rec.get("type") in ("user", "assistant"):
            out.append(rec)
    return out


def user_text(content) -> str:
    if isinstance(content, str):
        parts = [content]
    else:
        parts = [b.get("text", "") for b in content if b.get("type") == "text"]
    text = SYSTEM_REMINDER.sub("", "\n".join(parts)).strip()
    return text


def tool_result_text(block: dict) -> str:
    c = block.get("content")
    if isinstance(c, list):
        c = "\n".join(
            b.get("text", "[image]") if b.get("type") == "text" else f"[{b.get('type')}]"
            for b in c
        )
    return str(c or "").strip()


def render(records: list[dict], title: str) -> list[str]:
    md = [f"## {title}", ""]
    for rec in records:
        content = rec["message"]["content"]
        ts = rec.get("timestamp", "")[:19].replace("T", " ")
        if rec["type"] == "user":
            if rec.get("isCompactSummary"):
                md += [
                    f"### ⟳ Context summary ({ts} UTC)",
                    "",
                    "_The conversation ran out of context here; the agent continued from this "
                    "automatic summary of everything above._",
                    "",
                    "<details><summary>Show summary</summary>",
                    "",
                    fence(user_text(content)),
                    "",
                    "</details>",
                    "",
                ]
                continue
            text = user_text(content)
            if text:
                md += [f"### 👤 User ({ts} UTC)", "", text, ""]
            if isinstance(content, list):
                for b in content:
                    if b.get("type") == "tool_result":
                        res = tool_result_text(b)
                        label = "Tool error" if b.get("is_error") else "Result"
                        md += [
                            f"<details><summary>{label}</summary>",
                            "",
                            fence(clip(res, MAX_RESULT_LINES, MAX_RESULT_CHARS) or "(empty)"),
                            "",
                            "</details>",
                            "",
                        ]
        else:
            for b in content:
                if b.get("type") == "text" and b["text"].strip():
                    md += [f"### 🤖 Assistant ({ts} UTC)", "", b["text"].strip(), ""]
                elif b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                    inp = b.get("input", {})
                    desc = inp.get("description") if isinstance(inp, dict) else None
                    head = f"**🔧 {b['name']}**" + (f" — {desc}" if desc else "")
                    if isinstance(inp, dict) and set(inp) <= {"command", "description", "timeout"}:
                        body = fence(clip(inp.get("command", ""), MAX_INPUT_LINES), "bash")
                    else:
                        body = fence(clip(json.dumps(inp, indent=2), MAX_INPUT_LINES), "json")
                    md += [head, "", body, ""]
    return md


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("out_dir", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("sessions", nargs="+", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--subagent", action="append", type=Path, default=[])
    args = ap.parse_args()
    args.out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    seen: set[str] = set()  # a continued session repeats records of the one before it
    md = ["# AI agent session: Weather Risk Intelligence Agent", ""]
    raw: list[dict] = []
    for i, path in enumerate(args.sessions, 1):
        recs = [r for r in load_records(path) if r.get("uuid") not in seen]
        seen.update(r.get("uuid") for r in recs)
        md += render(recs, f"Part {i}")
        raw += recs
    for path in args.subagent:
        recs = load_records(path)
        md += render(recs, f"Sub-agent: {path.stem}")
        raw += recs

    for rec in raw:  # drop private reasoning from the raw log too
        content = rec["message"].get("content")
        if isinstance(content, list):
            rec["message"]["content"] = [b for b in content if b.get("type") != "thinking"]

    (args.out_dir / "transcript.md").write_text(redact("\n".join(md)) + "\n")
    with open(args.out_dir / "session.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for rec in raw:
            f.write(redact(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False)) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {len(raw)} records to {args.out_dir}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    ap.add_argument("sessions", nargs="+", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--subagent", action="append", type=Path, default=[])
    args = ap.parse_args()

"""Turn Claude Code session logs (.jsonl) into a readable, redacted Markdown transcript.

Usage:
    python docs/ai-session/export_session.py OUT_DIR SESSION.jsonl [SESSION2.jsonl ...]
        [--subagent AGENT.jsonl ...]

Writes, for the given session files (in order, as consecutive parts of one session):
    OUT_DIR/transcript.md       every user message, assistant reply and tool call, in order
    OUT_DIR/session.jsonl       the same records as raw JSON (user/assistant only), redacted

What is left out, and why:
  - Harness bookkeeping records (API request blobs, file snapshots, cost state): not part of
    the conversation, large, and they repeat the system prompt.
  - <system-reminder> blocks injected into user turns: automatic context, not the user's words.
  - The model's private reasoning ("thinking" blocks): only the visible conversation is shown.
  - Long tool outputs are cut to their first lines in the Markdown (the raw JSONL keeps
    them whole).

Redaction runs on everything written: API keys, the user's email, name and local username.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

# Replacement rules. Order matters: the full name before the username it contains.
REDACTIONS = [
    (re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}"), "[REDACTED_API_KEY]"),
    (re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@gmail\.com"), "[user-email]"),
    (re.compile(r"[redacted]", re.I), "[user]"),
    (re.compile(r"[redacted]", re.I), "user"),
    (re.compile(r"\b[redacted]1\b", re.I), "[github-user]"),
]
SYSTEM_REMINDER = re.compile(r"<system-reminder>.*?</system-reminder>", re.S)
MAX_RESULT_LINES, MAX_RESULT_CHARS = 40, 4000
MAX_INPUT_LINES = 80


def redact(text: str) -> str:
    for pattern, repl in REDACTIONS:
        text = pattern.sub(repl, text)
    return text


def clip(text: str, max_lines: int, max_chars: int = 10**9) -> str:
    lines = text.splitlines()
    out = "\n".join(lines[:max_lines])[:max_chars]
    hidden = len(lines) - max_lines
    if hidden > 0 or len(text) > max_chars:
        out += f"\n… [{max(hidden, 0)} more lines cut for readability; full text in session.jsonl]"
    return out


def fence(text: str, lang: str = "") -> str:
    # Use a fence longer than any backtick run inside, so nested code blocks can't break it.
    ticks = "`" * max(3, max((len(m) for m in re.findall(r"`+", text)), default=0) + 1)
    return f"{ticks}{lang}\n{text}\n{ticks}"


def load_records(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        try:
            rec = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if rec.get("type") in ("user", "assistant"):
            out.append(rec)
    return out


def user_text(content) -> str:
    if isinstance(content, str):
        parts = [content]
    else:
        parts = [b.get("text", "") for b in content if b.get("type") == "text"]
    text = SYSTEM_REMINDER.sub("", "\n".join(parts)).strip()
    return text


def tool_result_text(block: dict) -> str:
    c = block.get("content")
    if isinstance(c, list):
        c = "\n".join(
            b.get("text", "[image]") if b.get("type") == "text" else f"[{b.get('type')}]"
            for b in c
        )
    return str(c or "").strip()


def render(records: list[dict], title: str) -> list[str]:
    md = [f"## {title}", ""]
    for rec in records:
        content = rec["message"]["content"]
        ts = rec.get("timestamp", "")[:19].replace("T", " ")
        if rec["type"] == "user":
            if rec.get("isCompactSummary"):
                md += [
                    f"### ⟳ Context summary ({ts} UTC)",
                    "",
                    "_The conversation ran out of context here; the agent continued from this "
                    "automatic summary of everything above._",
                    "",
                    "<details><summary>Show summary</summary>",
                    "",
                    fence(user_text(content)),
                    "",
                    "</details>",
                    "",
                ]
                continue
            text = user_text(content)
            if text:
                md += [f"### 👤 User ({ts} UTC)", "", text, ""]
            if isinstance(content, list):
                for b in content:
                    if b.get("type") == "tool_result":
                        res = tool_result_text(b)
                        label = "Tool error" if b.get("is_error") else "Result"
                        md += [
                            f"<details><summary>{label}</summary>",
                            "",
                            fence(clip(res, MAX_RESULT_LINES, MAX_RESULT_CHARS) or "(empty)"),
                            "",
                            "</details>",
                            "",
                        ]
        else:
            for b in content:
                if b.get("type") == "text" and b["text"].strip():
                    md += [f"### 🤖 Assistant ({ts} UTC)", "", b["text"].strip(), ""]
                elif b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                    inp = b.get("input", {})
                    desc = inp.get("description") if isinstance(inp, dict) else None
                    head = f"**🔧 {b['name']}**" + (f" — {desc}" if desc else "")
                    if isinstance(inp, dict) and set(inp) <= {"command", "description", "timeout"}:
                        body = fence(clip(inp.get("command", ""), MAX_INPUT_LINES), "bash")
                    else:
                        body = fence(clip(json.dumps(inp, indent=2), MAX_INPUT_LINES), "json")
                    md += [head, "", body, ""]
    return md


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("out_dir", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("sessions", nargs="+", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--subagent", action="append", type=Path, default=[])
    args = ap.parse_args()
    args.out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    seen: set[str] = set()  # a continued session repeats records of the one before it
    md = ["# AI agent session: Weather Risk Intelligence Agent", ""]
    raw: list[dict] = []
    for i, path in enumerate(args.sessions, 1):
        recs = [r for r in load_records(path) if r.get("uuid") not in seen]
        seen.update(r.get("uuid") for r in recs)
        md += render(recs, f"Part {i}")
        raw += recs
    for path in args.subagent:
        recs = load_records(path)
        md += render(recs, f"Sub-agent: {path.stem}")
        raw += recs

    for rec in raw:  # drop private reasoning from the raw log too
        content = rec["message"].get("content")
        if isinstance(content, list):

12860:  "content": """"Turn Claude Code session logs (.jsonl) into a readable, redacted Markdown transcript.

Usage:
    python docs/ai-session/export_session.py OUT_DIR SESSION.jsonl [SESSION2.jsonl ...]
        [--subagent AGENT.jsonl ...]

Writes, for the given session files (in order, as consecutive parts of one session):
    OUT_DIR/transcript.md       every user message, assistant reply and tool call, in order
    OUT_DIR/session.jsonl       the same records as raw JSON (user/assistant only), redacted

What is left out, and why:
  - Harness bookkeeping records (API request blobs, file snapshots, cost state): not part of
    the conversation, large, and they repeat the system prompt.
  - <system-reminder> blocks injected into user turns: automatic context, not the user's words.
  - The model's private reasoning ("thinking" blocks): only the visible conversation is shown.
  - Long tool outputs are cut to their first lines in the Markdown (the raw JSONL keeps
    them whole).

Redaction runs on everything written: API keys, the user's email, name and local username.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

# Replacement rules. Order matters: the full name before the username it contains.
REDACTIONS = [
    (re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}"), "[REDACTED_API_KEY]"),
    (re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@gmail\.com"), "[user-email]"),
    (re.compile(r"[redacted]", re.I), "[user]"),
    (re.compile(r"[redacted]", re.I), "user"),
    (re.compile(r"\b[redacted]1\b", re.I), "[github-user]"),
]
SYSTEM_REMINDER = re.compile(r"<system-reminder>.*?</system-reminder>", re.S)
MAX_RESULT_LINES, MAX_RESULT_CHARS = 40, 4000
MAX_INPUT_LINES = 80


def redact(text: str) -> str:
    for pattern, repl in REDACTIONS:
        text = pattern.sub(repl, text)
    return text


def clip(text: str, max_lines: int, max_chars: int = 10**9) -> str:
    lines = text.splitlines()
    out = "\n".join(lines[:max_lines])[:max_chars]
    hidden = len(lines) - max_lines
    if hidden > 0 or len(text) > max_chars:
        out += f"\n… [{max(hidden, 0)} more lines cut for readability; full text in session.jsonl]"
    return out


def fence(text: str, lang: str = "") -> str:
    # Use a fence longer than any backtick run inside, so nested code blocks can't break it.
    ticks = "`" * max(3, max((len(m) for m in re.findall(r"`+", text)), default=0) + 1)
    return f"{ticks}{lang}\n{text}\n{ticks}"


def load_records(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        try:
            rec = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if rec.get("type") in ("user", "assistant"):
            out.append(rec)
    return out


def user_text(content) -> str:
    if isinstance(content, str):
        parts = [content]
    else:
        parts = [b.get("text", "") for b in content if b.get("type") == "text"]
    text = SYSTEM_REMINDER.sub("", "\n".join(parts)).strip()
    return text


def tool_result_text(block: dict) -> str:
    c = block.get("content")
    if isinstance(c, list):
        c = "\n".join(
            b.get("text", "[image]") if b.get("type") == "text" else f"[{b.get('type')}]"
            for b in c
        )
    return str(c or "").strip()


def render(records: list[dict], title: str) -> list[str]:
    md = [f"## {title}", ""]
    for rec in records:
        content = rec["message"]["content"]
        ts = rec.get("timestamp", "")[:19].replace("T", " ")
        if rec["type"] == "user":
            if rec.get("isCompactSummary"):
                md += [
                    f"### ⟳ Context summary ({ts} UTC)",
                    "",
                    "_The conversation ran out of context here; the agent continued from this "
                    "automatic summary of everything above._",
                    "",
                    "<details><summary>Show summary</summary>",
                    "",
                    fence(user_text(content)),
                    "",
                    "</details>",
                    "",
                ]
                continue
            text = user_text(content)
            if text:
                md += [f"### 👤 User ({ts} UTC)", "", text, ""]
            if isinstance(content, list):
                for b in content:
                    if b.get("type") == "tool_result":
                        res = tool_result_text(b)
                        label = "Tool error" if b.get("is_error") else "Result"
                        md += [
                            f"<details><summary>{label}</summary>",
                            "",
                            fence(clip(res, MAX_RESULT_LINES, MAX_RESULT_CHARS) or "(empty)"),
                            "",
                            "</details>",
                            "",
                        ]
        else:
            for b in content:
                if b.get("type") == "text" and b["text"].strip():
                    md += [f"### 🤖 Assistant ({ts} UTC)", "", b["text"].strip(), ""]
                elif b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                    inp = b.get("input", {})
                    desc = inp.get("description") if isinstance(inp, dict) else None
                    head = f"**🔧 {b['name']}**" + (f" — {desc}" if desc else "")
                    if isinstance(inp, dict) and set(inp) <= {"command", "description", "timeout"}:
                        body = fence(clip(inp.get("command", ""), MAX_INPUT_LINES), "bash")
                    else:
                        body = fence(clip(json.dumps(inp, indent=2), MAX_INPUT_LINES), "json")
                    md += [head, "", body, ""]
    return md


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("out_dir", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("sessions", nargs="+", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--subagent", action="append", type=Path, default=[])
    args = ap.parse_args()
    args.out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    seen: set[str] = set()  # a continued session repeats records of the one before it
    md = ["# AI agent session: Weather Risk Intelligence Agent", ""]
    raw: list[dict] = []
    for i, path in enumerate(args.sessions, 1):
        recs = [r for r in load_records(path) if r.get("uuid") not in seen]
        seen.update(r.get("uuid") for r in recs)
        md += render(recs, f"Part {i}")
        raw += recs
    for path in args.subagent:
        recs = load_records(path)
        md += render(recs, f"Sub-agent: {path.stem}")
        raw += recs

    for rec in raw:  # drop private reasoning from the raw log too
        content = rec["message"].get("content")
        if isinstance(content, list):
            rec["message"]["content"] = [b for b in content if b.get("type") != "thinking"]

    (args.out_dir / "transcript.md").write_text(redact("\n".join(md)) + "\n")
    with open(args.out_dir / "session.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for rec in raw:
            f.write(redact(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False)) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {len(raw)} records to {args.out_dir}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

12860:  "content": """"Turn Claude Code session logs (.jsonl) into a readable, redacted Markdown transcript.

Usage:
    python docs/ai-session/export_session.py OUT_DIR SESSION.jsonl [SESSION2.jsonl ...]
        [--subagent AGENT.jsonl ...]

Writes, for the given session files (in order, as consecutive parts of one session):
    OUT_DIR/transcript.md       every user message, assistant reply and tool call, in order
    OUT_DIR/session.jsonl       the same records as raw JSON (user/assistant only), redacted

What is left out, and why:
  - Harness bookkeeping records (API request blobs, file snapshots, cost state): not part of
    the conversation, large, and they repeat the system prompt.
  - <system-reminder> blocks injected into user turns: automatic context, not the user's words.
  - The model's private reasoning ("thinking" blocks): only the visible conversation is shown.
  - Long tool outputs are cut to their first lines in the Markdown (the raw JSONL keeps
    them whole).

Redaction runs on everything written: API keys, the user's email, name and local username.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

# Replacement rules. Order matters: the full name before the username it contains.
REDACTIONS = [
    (re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}"), "[REDACTED_API_KEY]"),
    (re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@gmail\.com"), "[user-email]"),
    (re.compile(r"[redacted]", re.I), "[user]"),
    (re.compile(r"[redacted]", re.I), "user"),
    (re.compile(r"\b[redacted]1\b", re.I), "[github-user]"),
]
SYSTEM_REMINDER = re.compile(r"<system-reminder>.*?</system-reminder>", re.S)
MAX_RESULT_LINES, MAX_RESULT_CHARS = 40, 4000
MAX_INPUT_LINES = 80


def redact(text: str) -> str:
    for pattern, repl in REDACTIONS:
        text = pattern.sub(repl, text)
    return text


def clip(text: str, max_lines: int, max_chars: int = 10**9) -> str:
    lines = text.splitlines()
    out = "\n".join(lines[:max_lines])[:max_chars]
    hidden = len(lines) - max_lines
    if hidden > 0 or len(text) > max_chars:
        out += f"\n… [{max(hidden, 0)} more lines cut for readability; full text in session.jsonl]"
    return out


def fence(text: str, lang: str = "") -> str:
    # Use a fence longer than any backtick run inside, so nested code blocks can't break it.
    ticks = "`" * max(3, max((len(m) for m in re.findall(r"`+", text)), default=0) + 1)
    return f"{ticks}{lang}\n{text}\n{ticks}"


def load_records(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    out = []
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        try:
            rec = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if rec.get("type") in ("user", "assistant"):
            out.append(rec)
    return out


def user_text(content) -> str:
    if isinstance(content, str):
        parts = [content]
    else:
        parts = [b.get("text", "") for b in content if b.get("type") == "text"]
    text = SYSTEM_REMINDER.sub("", "\n".join(parts)).strip()
    return text


def tool_result_text(block: dict) -> str:
    c = block.get("content")
    if isinstance(c, list):
        c = "\n".join(
            b.get("text", "[image]") if b.get("type") == "text" else f"[{b.get('type')}]"
            for b in c
        )
    return str(c or "").strip()


def render(records: list[dict], title: str) -> list[str]:
    md = [f"## {title}", ""]
    for rec in records:
        content = rec["message"]["content"]
        ts = rec.get("timestamp", "")[:19].replace("T", " ")
        if rec["type"] == "user":
            if rec.get("isCompactSummary"):
                md += [
                    f"### ⟳ Context summary ({ts} UTC)",
                    "",
                    "_The conversation ran out of context here; the agent continued from this "
                    "automatic summary of everything above._",
                    "",
                    "<details><summary>Show summary</summary>",
                    "",
                    fence(user_text(content)),
                    "",
                    "</details>",
                    "",
                ]
                continue
            text = user_text(content)
            if text:
                md += [f"### 👤 User ({ts} UTC)", "", text, ""]
            if isinstance(content, list):
                for b in content:
                    if b.get("type") == "tool_result":
                        res = tool_result_text(b)
                        label = "Tool error" if b.get("is_error") else "Result"
                        md += [
                            f"<details><summary>{label}</summary>",
                            "",
                            fence(clip(res, MAX_RESULT_LINES, MAX_RESULT_CHARS) or "(empty)"),
                            "",
                            "</details>",
                            "",
                        ]
        else:
            for b in content:
                if b.get("type") == "text" and b["text"].strip():
                    md += [f"### 🤖 Assistant ({ts} UTC)", "", b["text"].strip(), ""]
                elif b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                    inp = b.get("input", {})
                    desc = inp.get("description") if isinstance(inp, dict) else None
                    head = f"**🔧 {b['name']}**" + (f" — {desc}" if desc else "")
                    if isinstance(inp, dict) and set(inp) <= {"command", "description", "timeout"}:
                        body = fence(clip(inp.get("command", ""), MAX_INPUT_LINES), "bash")
                    else:
                        body = fence(clip(json.dumps(inp, indent=2), MAX_INPUT_LINES), "json")
                    md += [head, "", body, ""]
    return md


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("out_dir", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("sessions", nargs="+", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--subagent", action="append", type=Path, default=[])
    args = ap.parse_args()
    args.out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    seen: set[str] = set()  # a continued session repeats records of the one before it
    md = ["# AI agent session: Weather Risk Intelligence Agent", ""]
    raw: list[dict] = []
    for i, path in enumerate(args.sessions, 1):
        recs = [r for r in load_records(path) if r.get("uuid") not in seen]
        seen.update(r.get("uuid") for r in recs)
        md += render(recs, f"Part {i}")
        raw += recs
    for path in args.subagent:
        recs = load_records(path)
        md += render(recs, f"Sub-agent: {path.stem}")
        raw += recs

    for rec in raw:  # drop private reasoning from the raw log too
        content = rec["message"].get("content")
        if isinstance(content, list):
            rec["message"]["content"] = [b for b in content if b.get("type") != "thinking"]

    (args.out_dir / "transcript.md").write_text(redact("\n".join(md)) + "\n")
    with open(args.out_dir / "session.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for rec in raw:
            f.write(redact(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False)) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {len(raw)} records to {args.out_dir}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# AI agent session

This is the full working session with the AI coding agent (Claude Code, model Claude Opus 5.5)
that planned and built this project. It is a mandatory deliverable of the assignment.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [transcript.md](transcript.md) | **Start here.** The whole conversation in order: every user message, every assistant reply, and every tool call the agent made (shell commands, file edits, browser checks) with its result. Long outputs are folded. |
| [session.jsonl](session.jsonl) | The same conversation as raw JSON records, one per line, with full tool outputs. For tooling or for checking details. |
| [export_session.py](export_session.py) | The script that produced both files from Claude Code's local session logs. |

## How the session went

All times are UTC on 2026-11-23. Each stage ended with the agent explaining what it did and
why, and **pushing only after the user approved**, a rule the user set early in the session.

| Time | User request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 13:25 | Read the assignment PDF, plan the stages and tools, build in the repo step by step | 10-stage plan (`docs/PLAN.md`), stage 1 scaffold |
| 13:58 | Start stage 2 | Data layer: Open-Meteo, FEMA NRI and NWS clients, SQLite cache, ingest |
| 14:10 | "Before each push, explain what you did and why; add comments in the code" | Became a standing rule for the rest of the session |
| 14:13 | Start stage 3 | Deterministic scoring engine plus tests |
| 14:30 | Explain how the overall score is calculated | Explanation of the weighted averages and fixed scales |
| 14:34 | Change the weights: heat 10% to 5%, winter +2, flood +2, hurricane +1 | Weights updated in `config/scoring.yaml` |
| 14:59 | (API key added to `.env`) | Stage 4: Claude tool-use agent with JSON-schema output, tested live |
| 15:13 | Start stage 5 | FastAPI endpoints |
| 15:27 | Start stage 6 | Chat UI with voice input |
| 15:47 | Hide the "tools" badge; hide the ranking panel by default | UI changes |
| 15:51 | Start stage 7, then "Run it" | Evaluation set (17 cases), first run 15/17, 2 fixes, then 17/17 on re-run |
| 17:03 | (Context limit reached) | The agent continued from an automatic summary (shown folded in the transcript) |
| 17:45 | Start stage 8 | Risk-change alerts: snapshots, diff, webhook, daily scheduler |
| 18:01 | Deploy to Vercel plus a starting copy of the database | Built and committed locally, then reconsidered (next row) |
| 18:07 | Make a starting copy of the database; "keep starting copy only" | Kept the committed starting database and dropped the Vercel setup |
| 18:17 | Start stage 9 | `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, Dockerfile, `render.yaml` |
| 18:27 | Live URL on Render | Tested live: health, rankings, UI, a question and a follow-up |
| 18:32 | Start stage 10 | This export |

## Notes for the reader

- **Two parts.** The session hit the model's context limit twice. At 17:03 it continued from
  an automatic summary within the same log (Part 1). At 18:07 it continued in a new log file
  (Part 2). Part 2 repeats the end of Part 1, and the exporter removes those duplicates.
- **The Vercel detour.** At 18:01 the user asked for a Vercel deployment. The agent built and
  committed it. Back in the session, the user chose to keep only the starting database. The
  Vercel files were then removed in a follow-up commit, and the project deploys with Docker
  on Render instead. Both commits are in the git history.
- **One sub-agent.** During the Vercel work the agent ran one research helper agent. Its
  conversation is at the end of the transcript.
- **Grouped stages.** Stage numbers in the table follow `docs/PLAN.md`. Stage 4 (the agent)
  happened in the same stretch as the API-key message.

## What was removed or left out

- **Redacted:** API keys (none were ever printed, but the exporter checks), email addresses,
  and the user's name, username and GitHub handle. These are replaced with `[redacted]` or
  `[email]`. Local paths therefore read `/Users/[redacted]/...`.
- **Left out:**
  - Automatic context the app attaches to messages (`<system-reminder>` blocks);
  - the model's private reasoning ("thinking" blocks);
  - the app's internal bookkeeping records (API request logs, file snapshots).

  None of these are part of the visible conversation.
- **Shortened (Markdown only):** tool outputs longer than 40 lines are cut in
  `transcript.md`. `session.jsonl` keeps them whole.

## Regenerating

Claude Code keeps session logs in `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl`:

```bash
python docs/ai-session/export_session.py docs/ai-session PART1.jsonl PART2.jsonl \
  --subagent PART1/subagents/AGENT.jsonl --redact "Your Name" --redact yourusername
```

# Deploy a FastAPI app on Vercel

Deploy a FastAPI app to Vercel with the Python runtime and Vercel Functions.
Vercel looks for a `FastAPI` instance named `app` at supported entrypoints in
your repository.


<!-- docsgraph:related -->

- [Fastify on Vercel](https://vercel.com/docs/frameworks/backend/fastify) — Deploy Fastify applications to Vercel with zero configuration.

Full cross-link map for this page: [/docs/frameworks/backend/fastapi.graph.md](/docs/frameworks/backend/fastapi.graph.md)
<!-- /docsgraph:related -->

## Create or import your app

To move an existing FastAPI app from another platform, follow the Python API migration guide for [Heroku](/kb/guide/migrate-a-python-api-from-heroku-to-vercel), [Render](/kb/guide/migrate-a-python-api-from-render-to-vercel), or [Railway](/kb/guide/migrate-a-python-api-from-railway-to-vercel).

Create a FastAPI app or use an existing one:

### Get started with Vercel CLI

Initialize a new FastAPI project with the [Vercel CLI `init` command](/docs/cli/init):

```bash filename="terminal"
vc init fastapi
```

This clones the [FastAPI example repository](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/tree/main/examples/fastapi) in a directory called `fastapi`.

## Exporting the FastAPI application

To run a FastAPI application on Vercel, define an `app` instance that initializes `FastAPI` at a supported entrypoint:

- `app.py`, `index.py`, `server.py`, `main.py`, `wsgi.py`, or `asgi.py`
- the same filenames inside `src/` or `app/`

For example:

```py filename="app/main.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/")
def read_root():
    return {"Python": "on Vercel"}
```

To point Vercel to a FastAPI app in a custom module, set `tool.vercel.entrypoint` in `pyproject.toml`:

```toml filename="pyproject.toml"
[tool.vercel]
entrypoint = "backend.server:app"
```

The `tool.vercel.entrypoint` value tells Vercel to look for a `FastAPI` instance named `app` in `./backend/server.py`.

### Configure Python and dependencies

[Set the Python version](/docs/functions/runtimes/python/python-version) to match your application's dependencies. Vercel supports `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, and Pipenv manifests; see the [Python dependency configuration](/docs/functions/runtimes/python#dependencies) for supported lockfiles.

### Build command

The `build` property in `[tool.vercel.scripts]` defines the Build Command for FastAPI deployments. It runs after dependencies are installed and before your application is deployed.

```toml filename="pyproject.toml"
[tool.vercel.scripts]
build = "python build.py"
```

For example:

```py filename="build.py"
def main():
    print("Running build command...")
    with open("build.txt", "w") as f:
        f.write("BUILD_COMMAND")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

> **💡 Note:** If you define a [Build
> Command](https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json#buildcommand) in
> `vercel.json` or in the Project Settings dashboard, it takes precedence over a
> build script in `pyproject.toml`.

### Local development

Use `vercel dev` to run your application locally.

```bash filename="terminal"
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
vercel dev
```

> **💡 Note:** Minimum CLI version required: 48.1.8

### Deploying the application

Deploy the project by connecting your Git repository or by using the [Vercel CLI](/docs/cli/deploy):

```bash filename="terminal"
vc deploy
```

> **💡 Note:** Minimum CLI version required: 48.1.8

## Deploy without an account

To deploy your FastAPI app without an account or login, run this command in the project root:

```bash filename="terminal"
vercel deploy --temporary
```

The CLI builds the project, deploys it to production, and prints a claim URL. Claim the project to keep it live. See [Deploying without logging in](/docs/deployments/deploy-without-logging-in).

## Deploy with a frontend

Use [Vercel Services](/docs/services) to deploy a FastAPI backend and a frontend in one project. Follow the [Python backend with Next.js guide](/kb/guide/python-backend-on-vercel) to configure private backend calls, separate databases for each environment, and preview deployments across both apps.

### Build an agent app with eve

Deploy the [eve Agent with Python template](/templates/eve/eve-agent-with-python) to build a chat app with an eve agent, a Next.js frontend, and a FastAPI backend. The agent and frontend share a task list stored in Postgres, and the agent calls FastAPI endpoints to run Python tools for statistics and text analysis.

Vercel Services deploys all three services in one project. The FastAPI backend has no public route; the frontend and agent call it through [service bindings](/docs/services/bindings). See the [template repository](https://github.com/vercel-labs/eve-agent-python-template) for setup instructions and examples you can customize.

## Serving frontend and static assets

Vercel supports two methods for serving frontend and static assets with FastAPI.

### The `public/` directory

Place files in a `public/` directory at your project root. Vercel serves them
from the [CDN](/docs/cdn) at the matching root URL paths. For example,
`public/logo.svg` is served at `/logo.svg`. Default [response
headers](/docs/headers) apply unless you override them in `vercel.json`.

```py filename="app.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/favicon.ico", include_in_schema=False)
async def favicon():
    # /vercel.svg is served automatically from public/vercel.svg.
    return RedirectResponse("/vercel.svg", status_code=307)
```

> **💡 Note:** Do not mount the `public/` directory with `app.mount()`. Vercel handles it at the platform level.

### Built-in FastAPI frontend and static file support

When using [`app.frontend()`](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/frontend/) or
[`app.mount()`](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/sub-applications/) with [`StaticFiles`](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/static-files/),
files are promoted to the CDN at build time:

#### app.frontend

```py filename="app.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/api/hello")
def hello():
    return {"message": "Hello"}

app.frontend("/", directory="dist")
```

#### app.mount

```py filename="app.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

app = FastAPI()

app.mount("/assets", StaticFiles(directory="assets"), name="assets")
```

Promoted source directories are kept in the function bundle by default so the app can read from them at runtime. To exclude them and serve files from the CDN only, set `exclude = true`:

```toml filename="pyproject.toml"
[tool.vercel.fastapi.static]
exclude = true
```

See [Configuration](#configuration) for all available settings.

#### Route precedence for `app.mount()`

Files are served from the CDN at the mount's URL prefix. Route declaration order
determines which wins when a route and a CDN file share the same path:

- A route declared before the mount takes priority over CDN files. Matching
  requests reach the function.
- A route declared after the mount does not take priority. Matching requests are
  served from the CDN.

```python filename="main.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

app = FastAPI()

# Declared before the mount, so this route wins over any CDN file at this path.
@app.get("/static/protected.json")
def protected():
    return {"access": "denied"}

app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"))
```

The bare mount root (for example, `/static`) always reaches the function.
`StaticFiles` redirects it to the trailing-slash form.

#### Fallback behavior for `app.frontend()`

`app.frontend()` registers a low-priority frontend build. Every API route takes
priority over frontend files regardless of declaration order.

The `fallback` parameter controls CDN behavior when no file matches a request
under the mount:

| `fallback` value | File served | Status | When applied |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"auto"` | `404.html` if present, else `index.html` | `404` or `200` | See notes below |
| `"index.html"` | `index.html` | `200` | Navigation requests only |
| `"404.html"` | `404.html` | `404` | All misses |
| `None` | n/a | n/a | Unmatched paths reach the function |

An `index.html` fallback applies to navigation requests only: requests with an
explicit `text/html` or `application/xhtml+xml` `Accept` header and an
extension-less final URL segment (for example, `/dashboard` but not
`/dashboard/app.js`). All other misses reach the function. A `404.html` fallback
applies to every miss regardless of the `Accept` header. If `"auto"` is set but
neither file exists in the build directory, no fallback is applied.

Fallback routes apply to `GET` and `HEAD` requests only. All other methods
always reach the function.

#### Middleware

To redirect, rewrite, or answer requests before they reach FastAPI, use [Routing Middleware in Python](/docs/routing-middleware/python-reference). FastAPI middleware and dependency guards run inside the application, after a request reaches the function.

CDN-served files bypass the function entirely, so [middleware handlers](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/reference/fastapi/#fastapi.FastAPI.middleware) and [`Depends()`](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/reference/dependencies/) guards do not run for them.

Vercel detects these cases and keeps the affected static files and frontends in the function rather than promoting them to the CDN:

- **Top-level middleware**: All static mounts and frontends stay in the function.
- **Sub-app middleware**: Only that sub-app's mounts stay in the function. Mounts elsewhere are still promoted.
- **Frontend dependencies**: Frontends with [`Depends()`](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/reference/dependencies/) guards stay in the function.

Set `cdn = true` to promote files to the CDN even when middleware or dependency guards are present:

```toml filename="pyproject.toml"
[tool.vercel.fastapi.static]
cdn = true
```

#### Configuration

All settings go under `[tool.vercel.fastapi.static]` in `pyproject.toml`.

| Setting | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cdn` | omitted *(default)* | CDN promotion enabled. Disabled automatically when middleware or dependency guards are present. |
| `cdn` | `true` | CDN promotion always enabled, even when middleware or dependency guards are present. |
| `cdn` | `false` | CDN promotion disabled. All requests reach the function. |
| `exclude` | `false` *(default)* | Promoted source directories are kept in the function bundle. |
| `exclude` | `true` | Promoted source directories are excluded from the function bundle. |

## Startup and shutdown

You can use [FastAPI lifespan events](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/events/) to manage startup and shutdown logic, such as initializing and closing database connections.

```python filename="main.py"
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # Startup logic
    print("Starting up...")
    await startup_tasks()
    yield
    # Shutdown logic
    await cleanup_tasks()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
```

> **💡 Note:** Cleanup logic during shutdown is limited to a maximum of **500ms** after
> receiving the [SIGTERM
> signal](https://vercel.com/docs/functions/functions-api-reference#sigterm-signal).
> Logs printed during the shutdown step will not appear in the Vercel dashboard.

## Vercel Functions

When you deploy a FastAPI app to Vercel, it becomes a single [Vercel
Function](/docs/functions). Vercel uses [Fluid
compute](/docs/fluid-compute) by default, so the function scales with traffic.

To configure that function, add an entry to the [`functions`
object](/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json#functions) in `vercel.json` keyed by your
resolved entrypoint file. For example, to let an app defined in `app/main.py`
run for up to 60 seconds, set `maxDuration`:

```json filename="vercel.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json",
  "functions": {
    "app/main.py": {
      "maxDuration": 60
    }
  }
}
```

For more options, see [Configuring
functions](/docs/functions/configuring-functions) and the [`functions`
property](/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json#functions).

## Run background and scheduled tasks

To process work independently of an API response, enqueue tasks with [Celery](/docs/frameworks/backend/celery) or [Dramatiq](/docs/frameworks/backend/dramatiq). Both integrations use Vercel Queues to invoke worker functions, and their guides show how to enqueue work from a Python web application.

To use the Queues SDK directly, [process background jobs in Python with Vercel Queues](/kb/guide/python-and-vercel-queues). For a process that needs multiple steps, retries, or long waits, [build durable workflows in Python](/kb/guide/python-and-durable-workflows). Both guides start work from a FastAPI route.

For scheduled work, configure Cron Jobs to call a FastAPI route that runs the task or enqueues it. The [FastAPI cron job example](/kb/guide/ship-a-fastapi-app-on-vercel#run-scheduled-tasks-with-cron-jobs) includes the schedule and `CRON_SECRET` authorization check.

## Stream responses

Use FastAPI's `StreamingResponse` to send response chunks as they become available. See the [FastAPI streaming example](/kb/guide/ship-a-fastapi-app-on-vercel#stream-responses) for a generator-backed response on Vercel.

## Use WebSockets

Follow the [FastAPI WebSocket setup](/docs/functions/websockets#fastapi-with-asgi) to add a WebSocket endpoint. Connections follow function duration limits, so clients need to handle reconnects.

For a complete application, [build a multiplayer board with Next.js and FastAPI](/kb/guide/real-time-board-nextjs-fastapi). The guide uses Redis to coordinate presence and messages across function instances.

## Protect an internal API

Use Vercel Passport to require sign-in through your company's identity provider before requests reach your FastAPI app. Passport requires an Enterprise plan. Follow the [FastAPI Passport guide](/kb/guide/vercel-passport-backend-frameworks#fastapi) to verify visitor identity and authorize access within your app.

## Monitor and debug requests

Use [Runtime Logs](/docs/functions/logs) to inspect application output and errors, and [Observability](/docs/observability) to investigate request duration and failures. See [monitoring FastAPI with Observability](/kb/guide/ship-a-fastapi-app-on-vercel#monitor-performance-with-observability) for details.

## Limitations

All [Vercel Functions limitations](/docs/functions/limitations) apply to FastAPI applications, including:

- **Application size**: The FastAPI application becomes a single bundle, which has a standard bundle size limit of 500MB. [Large Functions](/docs/functions/limitations#large-functions-beta) support Python bundles up to 5GB on Fluid compute when enabled (public beta).

## More resources

For more about deploying FastAPI on Vercel, see:

- [FastAPI official documentation](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/)
- [Build with a FastAPI starter template](/kb/guide/build-with-a-fastapi-starter-template)
- [How to ship a FastAPI app on Vercel](/kb/guide/ship-a-fastapi-app-on-vercel)
- [Vercel Functions documentation](/docs/functions)
- [Backend templates on Vercel](https://vercel.com/templates?type=backend)

## Search the docs from your terminal

Search the Vercel docs and read pages as Markdown with the Vercel CLI. No login required.

```bash
# Find docs pages by keyword
npx vercel@latest docs search "environment variables"
npx vercel@latest docs search "function timeout"

# Print a docs page as Markdown, by path or URL
npx vercel@latest docs inspect <page>
```

# Using the Python Runtime with Vercel Functions

Use the Python runtime to run ASGI (Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface) and
WSGI (Web Server Gateway Interface) applications on Vercel. Vercel detects
supported Python frameworks and runs your application as Vercel Functions.


<!-- docsgraph:related -->
## Related pages

> **For AI agents:** Follow these links to understand how this page connects to the rest of the Vercel ecosystem. For the full cross-link map (inbound, outbound, prerequisites, and semantic neighbors), see the .graph.md link below.

- [How to ship a Flask app on Vercel](https://vercel.com/kb/guide/ship-a-flask-app-on-vercel) — Deploy a Flask app to Vercel with zero configuration. Learn how to ship from a template, the Vercel CLI, or Git, and con
- [Python 3.13 and 3.14 are now available ](https://vercel.com/changelog/python-3-13-and-3-14-are-now-available)

- [Deploy Python apps on Vercel using Docker ](https://vercel.com/kb/guide/vercel-docker-python-apps) — Deploy a Dockerized Python application that depends on native software, OCR engines, or small local models, plus a Next.

## Deploy with a Python framework preset

Vercel detects your framework automatically when it finds a matching dependency in
`requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, or `Pipfile`. The Python framework presets
work with [FastAPI](/docs/frameworks/backend/fastapi),
[Flask](/docs/frameworks/backend/flask),
[Django](/docs/frameworks/full-stack/django), and other Python web frameworks.
Define a supported Python entrypoint so Vercel can load your application.

Vercel then runs your app as Vercel Functions and routes every request to it,
so the app you run locally deploys as-is.

For framework-specific setup guides, see:

- [Deploy a FastAPI app on Vercel](/docs/frameworks/backend/fastapi)
- [Deploy a Flask app on Vercel](/docs/frameworks/backend/flask)
- [Deploy a Django app on Vercel](/docs/frameworks/full-stack/django)

## Migrate an existing Python API

To move an existing FastAPI, Flask, or Django API to Vercel, follow the migration guide for your current platform:

- [Migrate a Python API from Heroku to Vercel](/kb/guide/migrate-a-python-api-from-heroku-to-vercel)
- [Migrate a Python API from Render to Vercel](/kb/guide/migrate-a-python-api-from-render-to-vercel)
- [Migrate a Python API from Railway to Vercel](/kb/guide/migrate-a-python-api-from-railway-to-vercel)

## Combine Python with another framework

To run a Python backend and a frontend together in one project, you can use
[Services](/docs/services). Each part builds independently and routes to a
shared domain.

## Build with Vercel services

Use these guides to add storage, background processing, and AI capabilities to a Python application. Each guide includes a FastAPI example and deployment steps.

| Task                         | Guide                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Process background jobs      | [Process background jobs in Python with Vercel Queues](/kb/guide/python-and-vercel-queues)   |
| Store and serve files        | [Store and serve files from Python with Vercel Blob](/kb/guide/python-and-vercel-blob)       |
| Call third-party APIs        | [Call third-party APIs from Python with Vercel Connect](/kb/guide/python-and-vercel-connect) |
| Coordinate durable processes | [Build durable workflows in Python on Vercel](/kb/guide/python-and-durable-workflows)        |
| Execute untrusted code       | [Run untrusted Python code safely with Vercel Sandbox](/kb/guide/python-and-vercel-sandbox)  |
| Build AI agents              | [Build AI agents in Python with the AI SDK](/kb/guide/python-and-ai-sdk)                     |

## Python entrypoints

A Python entrypoint is the file and top-level variable that Vercel loads as the
Vercel Function handler. Vercel looks for a Python entrypoint in these
locations:

- `app.py`, `index.py`, `server.py`, `main.py`, `wsgi.py`, or `asgi.py`
- the same filenames inside `src/` or `app/`
- the module path configured with `tool.vercel.entrypoint` in `pyproject.toml`

For Django projects, Vercel also detects a `manage.py` file that sets
`DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE`, including in an immediate subdirectory, and resolves
the application from the `WSGI_APPLICATION` or `ASGI_APPLICATION` setting.

The entrypoint file must define one of these top-level names:

- `app` for most ASGI or WSGI frameworks, including FastAPI and Flask
- `application` for Django and other WSGI applications

To point Vercel to an app in a custom module, set `tool.vercel.entrypoint` to a
Python `module:variable` value:

```toml filename="pyproject.toml"
[tool.vercel]
entrypoint = "my_package.api:app"
```

*The \`tool.vercel.entrypoint\` value tells Vercel to load the \`app\` variable
from \`my\_package/api.py\`, which is also the key you'd use in
\`functions\`.*

Vercel still supports `[project.scripts] app = "module:variable"` for existing
projects. Use `tool.vercel.entrypoint` for new projects.

Here's a FastAPI example:

```python filename="app.py"
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/")
def home():
    return {"message": "Hello from Python on Vercel"}

@app.get("/api/items/{item_id}")
def read_item(item_id: int):
    return {"item_id": item_id}
```

```toml filename="pyproject.toml"
[project]
name = "my-python-api"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "fastapi>=0.117.1",
]
```

## Python version

Set the Python version for your project with `pyproject.toml`,
`.python-version`, or `Pipfile.lock`. For step-by-step instructions, see
[Set the Python version for your Vercel project](/docs/functions/runtimes/python/python-version).

If the required Python version is not defined or not supported, Vercel uses the
default version. The available versions are:

- **3.12** (default)
- **3.13**
- **3.14**

## Dependencies

Define dependencies in `pyproject.toml` (with or without a `uv.lock`),
`requirements.txt`, or a `Pipfile` with a corresponding `Pipfile.lock`.

```python filename="requirements.txt"
fastapi==0.117.1
```

*An example \`requirements.txt\` file that defines \`FastAPI\` as a dependency.*

## Streaming

Vercel Functions support streaming responses when using the Python runtime.
This lets you send parts of a response as they become ready.

## Controlling what gets bundled

By default, Python Vercel Functions include all files from your project that
are reachable at build time. There is no automatic tree-shaking for Python.

During deployment builds, Vercel automatically compiles Python source files
into bytecode and includes the resulting `.pyc` files in the function bundle
when space allows. This reduces initialization time and requires no
configuration.

Make sure your `pyproject.toml` or `requirements.txt` only lists packages
necessary at runtime. Explicitly exclude files you don't need to keep bundles
small and avoid hitting size limits.

> **💡 Note:** The standard Python bundle size limit is **500 MB** uncompressed.
> [Large Functions](/docs/functions/limitations#large-functions-beta)
> support Python bundles up to **5 GB** on Fluid compute when enabled (public beta).
> See the
> [bundle size limits](/docs/functions/limitations#bundle-size-limits)
> for details.

To exclude unnecessary files (tests, static assets, test data), configure
`excludeFiles` in `vercel.json` under the `functions` key. The pattern is a
[glob](https://github.com/isaacs/node-glob#glob-primer) relative to your
project root.

```json filename="vercel.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json",
  "functions": {
    "app.py": {
      "excludeFiles": "{tests/**,__tests__/**,**/*.test.py,**/test_*.py,fixtures/**,__fixtures__/**,testdata/**,sample-data/**,static/**,assets/**}"
    }
  }
}
```

*Exclude common development and static folders from a Python application to
stay under the 500 MB bundle limit.*

## Reading relative files

Python uses the current working directory when you pass a relative path to
[open()](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#open). The working
directory is the base of your project, not the directory containing the file.

## Routing Middleware

To redirect, rewrite, or answer requests before they reach your Python app, write [Routing Middleware](/docs/routing-middleware) in Python. Set `proxy` in `vercel.json` to a `module:attribute` entrypoint:

```json filename="vercel.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json",
  "proxy": {
    "entrypoint": "proxy:proxy"
  }
}
```

Your Routing Middleware runs separately from your app, with only the packages in the `vercel.proxy` dependency group installed. See the [Python reference](/docs/routing-middleware/python-reference).

## Existing projects using `/api`

Vercel supports existing projects that define file-based Python functions in
an `/api` directory. See [Python functions in the `/api`
directory](/docs/functions/runtimes/python/api-directory) for routing, handlers,
and configuration.

## Search the docs from your terminal

Search the Vercel docs and read pages as Markdown with the Vercel CLI. No login required.

```bash
# Find docs pages by keyword
npx vercel@latest docs search "environment variables"
npx vercel@latest docs search "function timeout"

# Print a docs page as Markdown, by path or URL
npx vercel@latest docs inspect <page>
```

Schedules

in the future. Schedules include timezones, private function and queue targets. You can also create schedules at runtime.

Migrate your Cron Jobs to Schedules

.

> Cron Jobs are available on all plans

Cron jobs are time-based scheduling tools used to automate repetitive tasks. By using a specific syntax called a [cron expression](#cron-expressions), you can define the frequency and timing of each task. This helps improve efficiency and ensures that important processes are performed consistently.

Some common use cases of cron jobs are:

- Automating backups and archiving them
- Sending email and Slack notifications
- Updating Stripe subscription quantities

Vercel supports cron jobs for [Vercel Functions](/docs/functions). Cron jobs can be added through [`vercel.json`](/docs/project-configuration) or the [Build Output API](/docs/build-output-api/configuration#crons).

See [Managing Cron Jobs](/docs/cron-jobs/manage-cron-jobs) for information on duration, error handling, deployments, concurrency control, and local execution. To learn about usage limits and pricing information, see the [Usage and Pricing](/docs/cron-jobs/usage-and-pricing) page.

A scheduled endpoint can enqueue a job or start a workflow when the work needs retries or durable execution. Compare [background worker options](/docs/background-workers) to choose how your scheduled work runs.

## Getting started with cron jobs

Learn how to set up and configure cron jobs for your project using our [Quickstart](/docs/cron-jobs/quickstart) guide.

## How cron jobs work

To trigger a cron job, Vercel makes an HTTP GET request to your project's production deployment URL, using the `path` provided in your project's `vercel.json` file. For example, Vercel might request the following endpoint to trigger a cron job: `https://*.vercel.app/api/cron`.

Vercel Functions triggered by a cron job on Vercel will always contain `vercel-cron/1.0` as the user agent. Each request also includes an `x-vercel-cron-schedule` header containing the cron expression that triggered the invocation (e.g., `0 5 * * *`). You can use this header to determine which schedule triggered your function when multiple cron jobs share the same path.

## Cron expressions

Vercel supports the following cron expressions format:

| Field        | Value Range     | Example Expression | Description                                          |
| ------------ | --------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Minute       | 0 - 59          | `5 * * * *`        | Triggers at 5 minutes past the hour                  |
| Hour         | 0 - 23          | `* 5 * * *`        | Triggers every minute, between 05:00 AM and 05:59 AM |
| Day of Month | 1 - 31          | `* * 5 * *`        | Triggers every minute, on day 5 of the month         |
| Month        | 1 - 12          | `* * * 5 *`        | Triggers every minute, only in May                   |
| Day of Week  | 0 - 6 (Sun-Sat) | `* * * * 5`        | Triggers every minute, only on Friday                |

### Validate cron expressions

To validate your cron expressions, you can use the following tool to quickly verify the syntax and timing of your scheduled tasks to ensure they run as intended.

You can also use [crontab guru](https://crontab.guru/) to validate your cron expressions.

### Cron expression limitations

- Cron jobs on Vercel do not support alternative expressions like `MON`, `SUN`, `JAN`, or `DEC`
- You cannot configure both day of the month and day of the week at the same time. When one has a value, the other must be `*`
- The timezone is always UTC

## More resources
